props.html: Factors that affect price

Prices can go up when: a wedding rather than a private party. A Saturday in June, September or October. A holiday weekend, which this market prices 20 to 30 percent above a standard date. A venue with a hard load-in, a long carry or a late curfew. A run of show with ceremony, cocktails, dinner and dancing all needing cover. A drive over the passes, and past them a night's lodging.

Price can go down when: Booked on an early weeknight. Fewer hours of performance time. A single set rather than the whole evening. A smaller build for the same music. A venue where the load-in is easy.
How signet puts together a live entertainment quote

Most acts in the Denver, Colorado market split their billing into two parts.

A call-out covers the evening commitment regardless of the length of the performance. It handles things like the drive, load-in, setup, sound check, strike, load-out and the production that comes along with all of it (in business parlance, they're the fixed costs).

Then a rate for performance time (these are like variable cost). That is why the price for an hour of cocktail entertainment is not strictly 1/4th the price of a 4 hour reception.

When comparing bookings, sound is the line item on a quote worth verifying the closest. With some acts, it's part of the total. With others, it shows up later as its own charge (or the venue is expected to have a system).
Travel and lodging are separate line items for us. Similarly, high-demand times like holiday weekends add a little extra to the bill.

The Denver, Colorado market prices for live entertainment bookings are set out in the cost guide, and we've got a corporate version, too that covers the types of entertainment companies book for client dinners, happy hours, and corporate events. That's covered in what live music costs for a corporate event.

props.html: Included for every act
Stage lighting and a dedicated engineer are optional, and quoted as their own line when you want them.
Quoted separately
Each of these arrives as its own line on the quote and on the contract, never folded into a total.
Save money: Booking more than one part of the night

Once one of our acts are on site, the drive is made, the sound system is up, and everyone is ready.

Covering the ceremony or the cocktail hour alongside the main booking is a cheaper way to fill the night than hiring twice.

How much of the night to cover is your call, and a smaller group early is a great answer as often as a bigger one later. If you would rather bring your own ceremony musician and use us to get people out onto the dance floor later, that's a common approach, too!
Tell us the flow of the evening when you send the date and we'll reply with availability and costs - maybe a few questions, too.
Common questions

Below are a few common questions about money and how Signet bills. Everything else, from player substitutions to decibel caps, is available on the full question list, and if you're curious about the wider, Colorado live entertainment market check out those answers in the cost guide.

items.q: What does a band cost for a corporate event in Denver?
items.a: In this market, a cover or jazz band for a corporate event can run $2,500 to $8,000, and a four to six piece band (the size the Denver market treats as its mid-tier), runs $4,000 to $6,000. Those are the market's figures. At Signet, we send you prices for the date and event when you enquire with us. Because, for example, mid-day on a Tuesday in September and Fourth of July weekend have significantly different demand.

We quote each date one-by-one. What's published on our site is a general market-view of what live music costs in Denver, Colorado. Send the date and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price for your night.

items.q: Do you provide a certificate of insurance?
items.a: Yes, we can, and also name your venue as additional insured, sent in the same email as the contract. The coverage limits match what Colorado venues write into their vendor requirements. Just let us know that's something you need.

items.q: How far in advance should we book?
items.a: Corporate holiday parties can be decided as far out as August, all the way through October for November, December and January dates. New Year's Eve books earliest of all - sometimes a year or more in advance. Weddings and galas can similarly be booked with more lead time - often 10 to 12 months, and 12 to 18 for a mountain venue or a fall Saturday. If your event is coming up sooner, no worries. Just reach out and we can often make something great work.
